title: Detecting and Mitigating Bias by Treating Fairness as a Symmetry Operation
summary: Machine learning systems deployed in high stakes socioeconomic settings routinely display bias. We formalize bias as a symmetry breaking operation: a classifier is fair if its outputs remain invariant under the counterfactual operation of switching a sensitive attribute, with merit features held fixed. We implement loss based regularization as a symmetry restoring mechanism and evaluate the framework on four synthetic datasets with varying levels of noise, correlation, and bias. The framework achieves upwards of 90\% violation reduction, with accuracy costs around 5\%. This framework does not require causal graph knowledge, is computationally lightweight, and generalizes to any sensitive attribute definable as a bit-flip, making it suitable for contexts where local sources of discrimination remain absent from mainstream benchmarks.

title: DiBS: Diffusion-Informed Branch Selection
summary: Sudoku is a representative constraint satisfaction problem that requires global structural reasoning under strict discrete constraints. The existing works of solving Sudoku mainly focus on two dominant approaches, i.e., traditional heuristic and deep learning solver. However, they suffer from two complementary limitations: learning-based solvers lack hard correctness guarantees, while complete symbolic solvers are still prone to long-tail search. To address these shortcomings, we propose a novel diffusion model-guided approach, termed as DiBS, for the branch selection search process. Specifically, DiBS keeps the symbolic solver complete and uses the diffusion model as a branch-ordering guide. The core method is ranking candidate values under the current partial assignment and lightweight consistency signal. Furthermore, we provide an in-depth theoretical proof to reveal how it works and why it works. Experiments on the challenging Royle 17-clue Sudoku benchmark show that our DiBS substantially reduces search cost relative to strong heuristic baselines, especially in nodes, backtracks, and long-tail percentiles. Besides, these results confirm that learned global guidance is effective on hard instances where branch-order mistakes are most expensive. All codes are available at https://github.com/shanxierdan/DiBS.

title: SafeGene: Reusable Adapters for Transferable Safety Alignment
summary: Open-weight LLMs are increasingly fine-tuned into customized assistants, but downstream fine-tuning can weaken safety alignment and make models more vulnerable to malicious prompts, even when the training data is not intentionally harmful. This creates a recurring safety recovery problem as target models are repeatedly updated with new task data or user interactions. We propose SafeGene, a reusable safety-adapter module designed for cross-task reuse within each architecture-compatible model family. Rather than treating safety recovery as a model-specific repair step, SafeGene treats safety capability as an independent, reusable adapter representation decoupled from task-specific updates. This representation is obtained from aligned--degraded model discrepancies, refined into task-transferable safety vectors through data-aware layer selection, and expressed in each downstream task-adapted model via few-shot layer-wise coefficient recalibration. Experiments across multiple model families, downstream tasks, and safety judges show that SafeGene-enhanced models reduce harmful response rates while maintaining downstream performance, outperforming representative safe adaptation methods in safety--utility trade-off.

summary: This paper examines the ethical implications of LLM intermediaries in housing search, focusing on algorithmic judgment, place identity, and the potential for racial steering. It highlights how LLMs can mediate access to housing information and recommendations, raising concerns about fairness.

title: RECAP: Regression Evaluation for Continual Adaptation of Prompts
summary: RECAP (Regression Evaluation for Continual Adaptation of Prompts) is presented as a method to ensure compliance in production agentic systems facing evolving constraints. It helps adapt prompts to new requirements without errors.

title: ShallowBench: Benchmarking Generative Drug Design Models on Shallow-Pocket Targets
summary: ShallowBench is introduced as a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating generative drug design models on challenging shallow-pocket targets. It addresses the current struggle of these models to design effective ligands for low-pocketability targets.

title: MSAIC-Net: A Multi-Scale Attention and Imbalance-Aware Contrastive Network for ECG-Based Myocardial Substrate Abnormality Detection
summary: This paper introduces MSAIC-Net, a Multi-Scale Attention and Imbalance-Aware Contrastive Network for ECG-based detection of myocardial substrate abnormalities. It offers a new method for detecting conditions like myocardial scar and infarction from ECG data.

title: Flatland: The Adventures of Gradient Descent with Large Step Sizes
summary: This paper investigates the largest possible step size for gradient descent in neural network training, especially for non-globally L-smooth objective functions.

title: Synthics: Synthetic Physics-like Datasets for Machine Learning
summary: This paper introduces 'Synthics,' a method for generating synthetic, physics-like datasets to improve machine learning model generalization when real-world data is limited.

title: Performance Variation in Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper studies the low run-to-run robustness and significant performance variation observed in deep reinforcement learning algorithms across independent runs.

title: A Rolling-Window Framework for Churn Prediction and Behavioral Driver Identification
summary: This paper proposes a rolling-window framework for predicting customer churn and identifying behavioral drivers, particularly in non-contractual service environments.

title: Federated Foundation Models over Vehicular Networks
summary: This paper presents a vision for integrating multi-modal multi-task federated foundation models into vehicular networks to leverage their power while preserving privacy.

title: Interpreting Learning Under Competing Models: Joint and Stepwise Approaches for Dynamic Cognitive Diagnosis
summary: This paper proposes joint and stepwise approaches for dynamic cognitive diagnosis to interpret learning and track skill mastery from data in digital learning environments.

title: SCALE: Scalable Cross-Attention Learning with Extrapolation for Agentic Workflow Scheduling
summary: This paper introduces SCALE, a method using cross-attention learning for scalable scheduling of tasks within agentic Large Language Model systems on heterogeneous clusters.

title: PandaAI: A Practical Agent CQ2 for Neuro-symbolic Data Analysis And Integrated Decision-Making in Quantitative Finance
summary: This paper proposes PandaAI, a practical agent leveraging Large Language Models for neuro-symbolic data analysis and integrated decision-making in quantitative finance.

title: Architecture Shapes Transfer Specificity in Implicit Neural Representations
summary: This paper investigates how the architecture of implicit neural representations, such as SIREN or ReLU MLPs, influences transfer specificity in coordinate networks.

title: Hearing the Unspoken: Language Model Priors for Acoustic Adversarial Attacks
summary: This paper explores how language model priors can be used to develop acoustic adversarial attacks against Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems.

title: The Geometry of Last-Layer Model Stealing
summary: This paper uses geometry to explain how the last layer of a machine learning model, specifically a transformer network, can be precisely stolen.

title: Modeling Nonlinear Feature Interactions with Product-Unit Residual Networks
summary: This paper investigates product-unit residual networks as a novel architecture for multilayer perceptrons to better model and interpret nonlinear feature interactions.

title: Product units in gated recurrent units improve nuclear-mass prediction
summary: This paper proposes using gated recurrent units with product units to improve the prediction of atomic nuclear masses, complementing theoretical models.

title: Evidence-Grounded Ensemble Diagnosis of 802.11 Packet Captures: A Multi-Stage Pipeline with Deterministic Reliability Scoring
summary: This paper presents a multi-stage pipeline for evidence-grounded diagnosis of 802.11 packet captures, addressing issues with existing LLM-based approaches.

title: GlucoFM-Bench: Benchmarking Time-Series Foundation Models for Blood Glucose Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces GlucoFM-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating and comparing time-series foundation models in blood glucose forecasting.

title: Data-Constrained Language Model Pretraining: Improved Regularization and Scaling Laws
summary: This paper re-examines scaling laws for language model pretraining under data-constrained conditions and proposes improved regularization techniques.

title: GRASP: Geometry-aware Residual Alignment for Scalable Pretraining Data Attribution
summary: This paper introduces GRASP, a geometry-aware method for scalable pretraining data attribution that accounts for critical subset dynamics like redundancy and complementarity.

title: TALAN: Task-Aligned Latent Adaptation Networks for Targeted Post-Training of Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces TALAN (Task-Aligned Latent Adaptation Networks) for targeted post-training of Large Language Models to improve specific abilities without degrading others.

title: The Fine-Tuning Trap: Evaluating Negative Transfer and the Role of PEFT in Sub-1B Mathematical Reasoning
summary: This paper evaluates fine-tuning strategies for sub-1B Small Language Models on mathematical reasoning, uncovering negative transfer and the role of PEFT methods.

title: From Sampled Outcomes to Capability Distributions: Rethinking Supervision for LLM Routing
summary: This paper proposes rethinking supervision for LLM routing by moving from single sampled outcomes to capability distributions, acknowledging the stochastic nature of LLM generation.

title: GenPO++: Generative Policy Optimization with Jacobian-free Likelihood Ratios
summary: This introduces GenPO++, a generative policy optimization method for reinforcement learning, enabling expressive and multimodal action distributions in complex continuous-control tasks.

title: Heterogeneous Effects of Green Finance on Urban Decarbonization: Evidence from 285 Cities in China
summary: This study uses econometric models and machine learning to analyze the heterogeneous effects of green finance on urban decarbonization in 285 Chinese cities, investigating its mechanisms and impact.

title: Accelerating Reproducible Research in Synthetic EHR Generation
summary: This paper addresses challenges in accelerating reproducible research for high-fidelity synthetic Electronic Health Record (EHR) generation, crucial for medical research while preserving patient privacy.

title: RASFT: Rollout-Adaptive Supervised Fine-Tuning for Reasoning
summary: This introduces RASFT (Rollout-Adaptive Supervised Fine-Tuning), a method for adapting large language models to reasoning tasks by learning from expert demonstrations in a more flexible way.

title: A Geometric View for Understanding Concept Learning and Neuron Interpretation in Sparse Autoencoders
summary: This paper proposes a mathematical framework for understanding concept learning and neuron interpretation in sparse autoencoders (SAEs), enhancing the interpretability of neural networks.

title: CF-JEPA: Mask-free forward prediction with asymmetric encoder utilization for time-series representation learning
summary: This introduces CF-JEPA, a mask-free forward prediction method with asymmetric encoder utilization for self-supervised time-series representation learning, addressing limitations of existing paradigms.

title: Hierarchical Forecast Reconciliation for Urban Rail Transit Demand Prediction under Operational Disruptions
summary: This research focuses on hierarchical forecast reconciliation for urban rail transit demand prediction, crucial for operational planning, especially under disruptive conditions.

title: Constructing VAE Latent Spaces with Prescribed Topology
summary: This work explores constructing Variational Autoencoder (VAE) latent spaces with prescribed topology to improve representation quality, especially when data lies on non-Euclidean manifolds.

title: Bias in Filter Feature Selection Evaluation: A Meta-Analysis of Datasets, Baselines, and Experimental Design Choices
summary: This meta-analysis examines bias in the evaluation of filter feature selection methods, reviewing datasets, baselines, and experimental design choices used for comparison.

title: SlimSearcher: Training Efficiency-Aware Web Agents via Adaptive Reward Gating
summary: This introduces SlimSearcher, a system for training efficiency-aware web agents that uses adaptive reward gating to reduce computational costs for complex information-seeking tasks.

title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper analyzes the training dynamics and parameter space trajectory of on-policy distillation (OPD), a method used to improve large language model reasoning, comparing it with SFT and RL.

title: OffQ: Taming Structured Outliers in LLM Quantization by Offsetting
summary: This proposes OffQ, a method for improving low-bit quantization in large language models by offsetting structured activation outliers to enhance inference acceleration and memory efficiency.

title: Learning Explicit Behavioral Models with Adaptive Questions and World-Model Probes
summary: This research focuses on enabling interactive agents to learn explicit behavioral models using adaptive questions and world-model probes, aiming for more robust and adaptable behavior.

title: Improving Cross-Lingual Factual Recall via Consistency-Driven Reinforcement Learning
summary: This introduces a method using consistency-driven reinforcement learning and the PolyFact dataset to improve cross-lingual factual recall in large language models.

title: Re-Centering Humans in LLM Personalization
summary: This paper studies the gap in LLM personalization performance when moving from synthetic to real user data, advocating for re-centering human preferences in personalization evaluations.

title: UnpredictaBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Distributional Randomness in LLMs
summary: This introduces UnpredictaBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of large language models to capture and reproduce true underlying distributional randomness.

title: How Language Models Fail: Token-Level Signatures of Committed and Persistent Reasoning Failures
summary: This research characterizes how large language models fail in reasoning, identifying distinct token-level signatures that reveal empirically distinguishable failure processes.

title: CAF-Gen: A Multi-Agent System for Enriching Argumentation Structures
summary: This introduces CAF-Gen, a multi-agent system designed to enrich argumentation structures by formalizing complex reasoning extracted from natural text in computational linguistics.

title: The Piggyback Hypothesis of Generalization: Explaining and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment
summary: This paper proposes the Piggyback Hypothesis to explain and mitigate emergent misalignment in LLMs, where fine-tuning on narrow tasks can cause broad misalignment in other domains.

title: What Do People Actually Want From AI? Mapping Preference Plurality
summary: This paper discusses the limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) in aligning LLMs, particularly regarding aggregating conflicting preferences and unrepresentative samples.

title: HKJudge: A Legal Discourse-Annotated Corpus for Interpreting What Courts Find, How They Reason, and What They Rule
summary: Introduces HKJudge, a new sentence-level expert-annotated corpus for legal discourse analysis of Hong Kong court judgments, aiming to interpret court findings, reasoning, and rulings.

title: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents
summary: Proposes a signal-driven observation method for long-horizon web agents to mitigate context degradation by decoupling observation frequency from action frequency, improving their reasoning over extended tasks.

title: Data-Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Models via On-Policy Distillation
summary: Investigates a data-efficient method called on-policy distillation to transform autoregressive language models into diffusion language models, avoiding pretraining from scratch.

title: Does Topic Sentiment Cause Perceived Ideology? Comparing Human and LLM Annotations in Political News Articles
summary: Compares human and LLM annotations on perceived political ideology in news articles to determine if topic sentiment has a causal effect, using Llama-3.3-70b-versatile for analysis.

title: Modular Monolingual Adaptation using Pretrained Language Models
summary: Proposes a modular adaptation technique for building monolingual language models for low-resource languages, leveraging pretrained language models through fine-tuning.

title: When to Think Deeply: Inhibitory Deliberation for LLM Reasoning
summary: Introduces IDPR, a framework for response-conditioned inhibitory deliberation, enabling large language models to selectively engage in deep reasoning, improving problem-solving efficiency and performance.

title: Evidence Graph Consistency in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Model-Dependent Analysis of Hallucination Detection
summary: Proposes using evidence graph consistency to improve hallucination detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, addressing limitations of existing methods that ignore structural relationships in retrieved evidence.

title: PromptPrint: Behavioral Biometrics Through Natural Language Prompting in LLMs
summary: Investigates "PromptPrint," a method to identify behavioral biometrics through natural language prompts to LLMs, exploring if short, task-driven prompts contain stable, author-identifiable signatures.

title: A Four-Condition Diagnostic Protocol for Evidence Utilization in Long-Context and Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
summary: Introduces a four-condition diagnostic protocol to evaluate whether long-context and retrieval-augmented language models genuinely utilize provided evidence, beyond simple accuracy or citation metrics.

title: When Better Codebooks Are Not Enough: Predictive Performance and Behavioral Reliability in LLM Political Event Coding
summary: Examines the predictive performance and behavioral reliability of large language models in political event coding for social science studies, assessing their faithfulness when using expert-written codebooks.

title: Explain Like I'm 5 or Whatever I Choose: Evaluating the Interactive Potential of Language Model Responses
summary: Evaluates the interactive potential of language model responses in scientific information seeking tasks, moving beyond static chat interfaces to assess multi-turn evaluations and new interface integrations.

title: TA-RAG: Tone-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Peer-Support Health Communication
summary: Introduces TA-RAG (Tone-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to enhance RAG systems for sensitive peer-support health communication by ensuring responses are not only factually grounded but also accessible, stigma-free, and empathetic.

title: Korean Culture into LLM Alignment: Toward Cultural Coherence
summary: Explores integrating Korean culture into large language model alignment, aiming for a constructive definition of culturally coherent responses beyond just suppressing undesirable outputs.

title: Progress-SQL: Improving Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-SQL via Progressive Rewards
summary: Introduces Progress-SQL, a method that improves reinforcement learning for text-to-SQL generation in large language models by using progressive rewards for iterative SQL correction.

title: The Dark Regulome: Disentangling Predictability from Regulation in Genomic Foundation Models
summary: Investigates the "dark regulome" in genomic foundation models to disentangle predictability from regulation in synaptogenic gene expression within high-grade gliomas.

title: Translate-R1: Cost-Aware Translation Tool Use via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces Translate-R1, a reinforcement learning method for cost-aware translation tool use, aiming to bridge the language performance gap in large language models by effectively integrating translation capabilities.

title: CRAFT: A Unified Counterfactual Reasoning Framework for Tabular Question Answering and Fact Verification
summary: Proposes CRAFT, a unified counterfactual reasoning framework designed to improve large language models' performance in tabular question answering and fact verification tasks requiring multi-step inference.

title: Interpreting Brain Responses to Language with Sparse Features from Language Models
summary: Uses sparse features from language models to interpret human brain responses to language, aiming to characterize the features represented by the human language cortex in cognitive neuroscience.

title: Are Large Language Models Suitable for Graph Computation? Progress and Prospects
summary: Explores the suitability of large language models for graph computation tasks, discussing their progress, limitations, and future prospects in reasoning over structured relationships and algorithmic operations.

title: An Expanded Synthetic Conversation Dataset for Multi-Turn Smishing Detection
summary: Introduces an expanded synthetic conversation dataset for multi-turn smishing detection, building on prior work (COVA) to establish and improve baseline detection benchmarks across various models.

title: EASE-TTT: Evidence-Aligned Selective Test-Time Training for Long-Context Question Answering
summary: Introduces EASE-TTT, a new method for Evidence-Aligned Selective Test-Time Training designed to improve long-context question answering for smaller language models by leveraging existing evidence within the input.

title: ThinkBooster: A Unified Framework for Seamless Test-Time Scaling of LLM Reasoning
summary: Presents ThinkBooster, a unified framework for test-time compute scaling that enhances large language model (LLM) reasoning by allocating additional compute during inference.

title: Didact: A Cross-Domain Capability Discovery System for Defence
summary: Introduces Didact, a cross-domain system designed for the defense sector to monitor rapidly evolving research and discover relevant priorities from fragmented, heterogeneous data sources.

title: Auditing Training Data in Domain-adapted LLMs: LoRA-MINT
summary: Presents LoRA-MINT, a new methodology for Membership Inference Test (MINT) designed to audit training data of domain-adapted large language models fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA).

title: OpenHalDet: A Unified Benchmark for Hallucination Detection across Diverse Generation Scenarios
summary: Introduces OpenHalDet, a unified benchmark for hallucination detection across diverse large language model generation scenarios, addressing inconsistencies in existing evaluation methods and improving domain coverage.

title: Tree-of-Experience: A Structured Experience-Management Solution for Self-Evolving Agents under Low-Repetition and Implicit-Reward Environments
summary: Presents Tree-of-Experience, a structured experience-management solution designed to enable self-evolving LLM agents to operate effectively in challenging environments with low-repetition tasks and implicit rewards.

title: Contrastive Training with LLM-generated Near-Misses for Robust Code-Switching Speech Recognition
summary: Proposes a Point-of-Interest (POI)-aware contrastive training framework that utilizes LLM-generated "near-misses" to enhance the robustness of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) for code-switching languages.

title: Principles of Concept Representation in Sentence Encoders
summary: Investigates the principles of concept representation in sentence encoders, focusing on representational compositionality and how their latent spaces facilitate low-distortion realizations of semantic operators.

title: MADE: Beyond Scoring via a Multilingual Agentic Diagnosing Engine for Fine-Grained Evaluation Insights
summary: Introduces MADE (Multilingual Agentic Diagnosing Engine), an agentic system designed to provide fine-grained evaluation insights beyond simple scores for multilingual and multicultural benchmarks.

title: Beyond Rubrics: Exploration-Guided Evaluation Skills for Reward Modeling
summary: Proposes a method for open-ended reward modeling that utilizes exploration-guided evaluation skills, moving beyond rubric-based approaches to address situations where verifiable answers are unavailable.

title: TRACE: Trajectory Reasoning through Adaptive Cross-Step Evidence Aggregation for LLM Agents
summary: Introduces TRACE, a method for Trajectory Reasoning through Adaptive Cross-Step Evidence Aggregation, designed to detect hidden malicious objectives in LLM agents by analyzing sequences of individually benign actions.

title: Modeling semantic association in self-paced reading with language model embeddings
summary: Explores the use of language model (LM) embeddings to quantify and model semantic association in self-paced reading, highlighting its importance for reading comprehension.

title: mmPISA-bench: Do LLMs Reason Equally Well Across 43 Languages?
summary: Introduces mmPISA-bench, a compact, high-quality multilingual reasoning benchmark derived from the OECD PISA assessment, designed to evaluate large language models across 43 languages.

title: SigmaScale: LLM Compression with SVD-based Low-Rank Decomposition and Learned Scaling Matrices
summary: Presents SigmaScale, a new method for large language model (LLM) compression that utilizes Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based low-rank decomposition combined with learned auxiliary scaling matrices.

title: Learning Perspectivist Social Meaning via Demographic-Conditioned Fusion Embeddings
summary: Proposes a method for learning perspectivist social meaning in language using demographic-conditioned fusion embeddings, acknowledging and modeling variations across annotator backgrounds and ideological positions.

title: Explicit Evidence Grounding via Structured Inline Citation Generation
summary: Introduces FullCite, a framework for generating structured inline citations to achieve explicit evidence grounding, thereby improving factualness and attribution in AI-generated content.

title: UrduMMLU: A Massive Multitask Benchmark for Urdu Language Understanding
summary: Introduces UrduMMLU, a new massive multitask benchmark comprising 26,431 Urdu multiple-choice questions across 26 subjects, designed for evaluating large language models in Urdu language understanding.

title: Geometry of Semantic Space: Comparative Study of Discrete and Continuous Models
summary: Presents a comparative study examining the semantic geometry of NLP models, analyzing supervised vector embeddings against lexical co-occurrence graphs to understand concept representation.

title: From Correctness to Utility: Gain-Based Prefix Evaluation for LLM Reasoning
summary: Proposes a gain-based prefix evaluation method for large language model (LLM) reasoning, which assesses a prefix's utility by how much it increases the probability of problem-solving rather than just its correctness.

title: Adversarial Creation and Detection of AI-Generated Social Bot Content
summary: Investigates the adversarial creation and detection of AI-generated social bot content, focusing on methodologies to combat the manipulation of information ecosystems despite the scarcity of ground-truth data.

title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
summary: This paper evaluates the sensitivity of Large Language Models to subtle prompt variations when used in healthcare applications, highlighting potential risks due to inconsistent performance.

title: KIT's Submission to Cross-Lingual Voice Cloning in IWSLT 2026
summary: This submission details KIT's approach to cross-lingual voice cloning for the IWSLT 2026 challenge, aiming to generate speech in a target language while preserving speaker identity.

title: Phun-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Phonological Understanding in Chinese
summary: Phun-Bench is introduced as a new benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models' phonological understanding in Chinese, an area often overlooked by existing semantic and spelling-focused benchmarks.

title: SV-Detect: AI-generated Text Detection with Steering Vectors
summary: SV-Detect proposes a novel method for detecting AI-generated text using steering vectors extracted from frozen language models, enhancing robustness against distribution shifts and editing attacks.

title: LLM-Guided Evolution for Medical Decision Pipelines
summary: This research explores using LLM-guided MAP-Elites evolution as an inference-time alternative for discovering and adapting medical decision strategies to clinical workflows.

title: M$^3$Exam: Benchmarking Multimodal Memory for Realistic User-Agent Interactions
summary: M$^3$Exam is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal memory and reasoning capabilities of language agents in realistic user-agent interactions, particularly with authentic file content and concealed information.

title: The Masked Advantage: Uncovering Local-Language Access to Cultural Knowledge in LLMs
summary: This research investigates how Large Language Models access cultural knowledge across different languages, critically examining existing evaluations and whether local language or English provides better access.

title: Sycophantic Praise: Evaluating Excessive Praise in Language Models
summary: This paper identifies sycophantic praise as a distinct alignment problem in language models, arguing that current methods are insufficient to reliably measure this form of explicit flattery.

title: Supervision versus Demonstration-Based In-Context Learning for Multiword Expression Classification
summary: This research compares supervision-based and demonstration-based in-context learning for multiword expression classification, specifically addressing challenging Turkish idiomatic light verb constructions.

title: Your UnEmbedding Matrix is Secretly a Feature Lens for Text Embeddings
summary: This paper investigates why large language models perform suboptimally as off-the-shelf embedding models, proposing that their unembedding matrix functions as a feature lens for text embeddings.

title: Applying Deep Learning for cockpit segmentation in the context of mixed reality
summary: This research applies deep learning techniques for cockpit segmentation within mixed reality environments, leveraging advances in computer vision for first-person view technologies.

title: GOPAgen: Motion-Aware and Efficient Agentic Long-Video Understanding with Structural Memory and Hierarchical Reasoning
summary: GOPAgen is introduced as a novel agentic system for motion-aware and efficient long-video understanding, integrating video codecs with structural memory and hierarchical reasoning capabilities.

title: WorldBench: A Challenging and Visually Diverse Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark
summary: WorldBench is presented as a challenging and visually diverse multimodal reasoning benchmark, designed to evaluate models' reliability across diverse settings and open-ended visual inputs.

title: Direct 3D-Aware Object Insertion via Decomposed Visual Proxies
summary: This paper presents a method for direct 3D-aware object insertion into images using decomposed visual proxies, providing explicit control over the object's 3D pose beyond 2D inpainting.

title: From Pixels to Newtons: Predicting In Vivo Joint Contact Forces from Monocular Video
summary: This research presents a method for predicting in vivo joint contact forces directly from monocular video, offering a non-invasive alternative for biomedical applications such as implant longevity and rehabilitation.

title: Inside the Visual Mind: Neuroscience-Motivated Concept Circuits for Interpreting and Steering Vision Transformers
summary: This research proposes using neuroscience-motivated concept circuits and sparse autoencoders to interpret and steer Vision Transformers, aiming to understand their inner workings for safer and more reliable deployment.

title: MMBU: A Massive Multi-modal Biomedical Understanding Benchmark to Probe the Perception Capabilities of Vision-Language Models
summary: MMBU is introduced as a massive multi-modal biomedical understanding benchmark designed to rigorously probe the fine-grained visual perception capabilities of Vision-Language Models for biomedical imaging tasks.

title: USU-Corn-WeedDB: A UAV RGB Image Dataset for Multi-Species Weed Detection in Forage Corn
summary: USU-Corn-WeedDB is a new public UAV RGB image dataset for multi-species weed detection in forage corn, addressing the scarcity of field-representative training data for site-specific weed management systems.

title: Anchored, Not Graded: Vision-Language Models Fail at Slant-from-Texture Perception
summary: This research demonstrates that Vision-Language Models fail to accurately perceive surface slant from texture in a graded manner, highlighting a specific limitation in their perceptual competence compared to humans.

title: MedSIGHT: Towards Grounded Visual Comprehension in Medical Large Vision-Language Models
summary: MedSIGHT proposes an approach towards achieving grounded visual comprehension in Medical Large Vision-Language Models, aiming to unify vision-language comprehension and medical image segmentation for clinically sound reasoning.

title: Breaking the Lock-in: Diversifying Text-to-Image Generation via Representation Modulation
summary: This paper introduces a method to diversify samples generated by text-to-image models, which typically produce similar outputs for a fixed prompt, using representation modulation.

title: VideoSEG-O3: A Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation
summary: This paper presents VideoSEG-O3, a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework designed to improve reasoning video object segmentation by integrating temporal, spatial, and linguistic understanding for precise pixel-level localization.

title: AdaGRPO: A Capability-Aware Adaptive Enhancement for Flow-based GRPO
summary: AdaGRPO proposes a capability-aware adaptive enhancement for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to improve the alignment of text-to-image flow models with human preferences, addressing limitations in the existing learning loop.

title: CFRNet: Cycle-Consistent Fixed-Point Training for Real-Time Blind Face Restoration on Consumer Embedded NPUs
summary: CFRNet introduces a cycle-consistent fixed-point training method for real-time blind face restoration on consumer embedded NPUs, balancing image quality with speed and memory constraints.

title: MotionEnhancer: Leveraging Video Diffusion for Motion-Enhanced Vision-Language Models
summary: MotionEnhancer leverages video diffusion techniques to improve Vision-Language Models' capability to capture fine-grained motion details for enhanced video understanding, addressing current limitations in event or story-level analysis.

title: LRMIL: Efficient Low-Resolution Multiple Instance Learning via High-Resolution Knowledge Distillation for Whole Slide Image Classification
summary: LRMIL proposes an efficient low-resolution multiple instance learning method for whole slide image classification in digital pathology, utilizing high-resolution knowledge distillation to overcome the computational demands of existing MIL approaches.

title: Multi-FRuGaL: Multimodal Flexible Redundancy-aware Decomposed Gated Learning for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis
summary: Multi-FRuGaL presents a multimodal flexible redundancy-aware decomposed gated learning approach for cancer diagnosis and prognosis, designed to effectively integrate heterogeneous and often incomplete patient data from various sources.

title: EgoPressDiff: Multimodal Video Diffusion for Egocentric UV-Domain Hand-Pressure Estimation
summary: EgoPressDiff introduces a multimodal video diffusion method for egocentric UV-domain hand-pressure estimation, aiming to improve accuracy and temporal consistency for applications in AR/VR, robotic imitation, and ergonomics.

title: Unified Safe In-context Image Generation in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers via Restricting Unsafe Information Flows
summary: This paper proposes a unified approach for safe in-context image generation in multimodal Diffusion Transformers by restricting unsafe information flows, aiming to prevent the creation of harmful content, particularly in image-to-image editing.

title: FreeAnimate: Training-Free Human Image Animation with Preview-Guided Denoising
summary: FreeAnimate introduces a training-free human image animation method that leverages preview-guided denoising, aiming to improve generalization and accessibility compared to existing diffusion models that require substantial training data.

title: ARAPDiffusion: ARAP Regularization for Diffusion-Based Deformable Shape Space Learning
summary: ARAPDiffusion introduces a latent diffusion model that incorporates as-rigid-as-possible (ARAP) deformation regularization to learn continuous shape spaces from deformable shape collections.

title: Diagnosing Visual Ignorance in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research diagnoses visual ignorance in Vision-Language Models, studying how they rely on language priors over visual evidence and the internal mechanisms and impact of this behavior on benchmark evaluations.

title: Stream3D-VLM: Online 3D Spatial Understanding with Incremental Geometry Priors
summary: Stream3D-VLM presents an online 3D vision-language model that enables real-time 3D spatial understanding from streaming video by utilizing incremental geometry priors.

title: LUCID: Learning Unified Control for Image Deflaring and Exposure Mastery in Nighttime Photography
summary: LUCID introduces a method for learning unified control for image deflaring and exposure mastery in nighttime photography, aiming to address competing degradations like intense flares and noise in low-light conditions.

title: Beyond Skeletons: Learning Animation Directly from Driving Videos with Same2X Training Strategy
summary: This paper introduces a "Same2X" training strategy to learn human image animation directly from driving videos, aiming to overcome limitations and errors caused by intermediate pose estimators, especially under occlusion.

title: DRIFT: From Robustness Gaps to Invariance Manifolds for AI-Generated Image Detection
summary: DRIFT proposes a method for detecting AI-generated images by analyzing robustness gaps and invariance manifolds in frozen vision foundation models, aiming to improve detection capabilities in open-world settings with unseen generators.

title: SVHighlights: Towards Extremely Long Sport Video Highlight Detection
summary: This paper introduces SVHighlights, the first benchmark specifically designed for highlight detection in extremely long sport videos, aiming to address the limitations of existing methods focused on short-form content.

title: When CLIP Sees More, It Fights Back Harder: Multi-View Guided Adaptive Counterattacks for Test-Time Adversarial Robustness
summary: This paper proposes multi-view guided adaptive counterattacks to improve the test-time adversarial robustness of Vision-Language Models like CLIP, which are otherwise vulnerable to adversarial perturbations despite their strong zero-shot recognition.

title: SS-TPT: Stability and Suitability-Guided Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Adversarially Robust Vision-Language Models
summary: SS-TPT introduces a stability and suitability-guided test-time prompt tuning method to enhance the adversarial robustness of Vision-Language Models like CLIP, addressing the impractical slowdowns and robustness-through-averaging limitations of prior adaptation defenses.

title: When is 3D Worth It? A Resource-Performance Frontier for CNNs and Transformers in Lung CT
summary: This paper investigates the resource-performance frontier for CNNs and Transformers in lung CT analysis, evaluating when 3D models provide sufficient performance gains to justify their increased computational cost and complexity over 2D or 2.5D approaches.

title: From Vision to Text: A Compact Multimodal Approach for Robust, Cross-Domain Presentation Attack Detection on ID Cards
summary: This paper proposes a compact multimodal model that combines visual and textual data for Presentation Attack Detection on ID cards, using new generative and discriminative blocks.

title: CL-CLIP: CLIP-Based Continual Learning Framework with Cost-Volume Category Decoupling for Object Detection
summary: This paper presents CL-CLIP, a CLIP-based continual learning framework that enables object detectors to acquire new categories over time while retaining previously learned ones.

title: Don't Pause: Streaming Video-Language Synchrony for Online Video Understanding
summary: This work addresses the challenge of online Video-LLMs pausing perception during response generation in streaming scenarios, aiming for seamless human-AI interaction.

title: GuideCAD: A Lightweight Multimodal Framework for 3D CAD Model Generation via Prefix Embedding
summary: This paper introduces GuideCAD, a lightweight multimodal framework that uses semantically rich visual-textual representations and prefix embedding to generate 3D CAD models.

title: Never Seen Before: Benchmarking Genuine Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval with Consistent Video-Sourced Datasets
summary: This research benchmarks Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval (ZS-CIR) with new consistent video-sourced datasets, addressing issues of irrelevance in existing datasets.

title: ForensicConcept: Transferable Forensic Concepts for AIGI Detection
summary: This paper proposes ForensicConcept, a framework for AI-generated image detection that aims to provide transferable forensic concepts to understand the evidence driving detection decisions.

title: STREAM: Stochastic Riemannian Flow Matching with Anisotropic Decoder for Digital Histopathology Image Generation
